scenario: Community search over short user-generated posts, questions and comments, focusing on relevance, nDCG and CTR.

papers.title: Optimal Fusion Weights Form Intervals, Not Points: A Latency-Aware Study of Query-Adaptive WRRF
papers.authors: Iris Ma, Zahra Shekarchi, Stuart Mcilroy, Mahtab Farrokh, Fattane Zarrinkalam, Joel Stremmel
papers.summary: Adaptive fusion need not predict one exact weight. Across 128 configurations, 74 significantly outperform standard RRF after multiple-testing correction.
papers.key_insight: Treat optimal weights as sets rather than arbitrary point targets, and include predictor latency in deployment decisions.

papers.title: Preference Is Not Position: Evaluating Reranking on NevIR in Fixed Hybrid Candidate Pools
papers.authors: Yuning Bian, Lele Xu, Yifan Yuan, Xinyu Yin, Chengyan Zhan
papers.summary: Correct pairwise preference does not guarantee a useful list position. Bounded Qwen3 reranking reaches preferred-passage MRR of 0.7509 in fixed hybrid pools.
papers.key_insight: Evaluate pair preference and full-list position separately; optimizing one can degrade the other.

papers.title: Cross-Pollination Retrieval: Finding Transferable Ideas Across Fields in Scientific Literature
papers.authors: Seokwon Jung, Yerang Kim, Yejin Kim, Alexander Rubinstein, Arnas Uselis, Sangwoo Park, Seong Joon Oh, Sangdoo Yun
papers.summary: Cross-topic citations teach retrieval models to find transferable ideas. Contrastive training raises Recall@10 from the best untrained retriever’s 0.26 to as high as 0.70.
papers.key_insight: Training labels define relevance. Topic similarity alone can miss useful analogies and may impair cross-domain retrieval.

papers.title: Beyond Recall Saturation: Scaling Hard-Negative Reranker Training for Industrial Legal Retrieval
papers.authors: Yunhan Li, Mingjie Xie, Zeyang Shi, Gengshen Wu, Min Yang
papers.summary: A two-stage hard-negative pipeline improves legal reranking after candidate recall saturates. The trained model wins 72.4% of non-tied internal offline preference comparisons.
papers.key_insight: Separate candidate recall from reranker quality. More dynamic mining stages do not consistently improve held-out performance.

papers.title: Conditional information Retrieval for Longitudinal Survey Harmonisation
papers.authors: Wing Yan Li, Zeqiang Wang, Michelle Lin, Jon Johnson, Suparna De
papers.summary: Concept-conditioned retrieval separates wording overlap from shared survey constructs. MAP and recall improve by roughly 2–3 points over baselines.
papers.key_insight: Explicit concepts can disambiguate semantic matching, and a general domain thesaurus can provide supervision when task labels are scarce.

papers.title: MemRevise: A Self-Revising Memory for Conversational Search
papers.authors: Mohammed Ali, Abdelrahman Abdallah, Adam Jatowt
papers.summary: A revisable topic memory tracks additions, abandonment and reactivation. With a frozen retriever, MemRevise reaches mean MRR@10 of 0.701.
papers.key_insight: Keep topic state transitions explicit so abandoned constraints stop affecting search while remaining recoverable.

papers.title: StrucChunk: Structure-Aware Retrieval for Legal Document RAG
papers.authors: Surya Deep Singh, Ashutosh Tripathi, Gaurav Deep Singh
papers.summary: Structure-aware legal chunking preserves clause boundaries and resolves cross-references before hybrid retrieval. LegalBench-RAG character Recall@8 reaches 48.18%.
papers.key_insight: Chunk boundaries determine whether evidence is representable at all; preserve document structure before tuning retrieval models.

papers.title: MEMORA: A Memory-Enhanced Multimodal Committee Reranking Agent for Reasoning-Intensive Retrieval
papers.authors: Mohamed Mahmoud, Mostafa Farouk Senussi, Mahmoud Abdalla, Mahmoud SalahEldin Kasem, Abdelrahman Abdallah, Hyun Soo Kang
papers.summary: MEMORA decomposes queries into factors, gathers evidence and combines committee verdicts with episodic memory. Text-to-text nDCG@10 reaches 41.5 on MM-BRIGHT.
papers.key_insight: A factor-level evidence matrix makes reranking decisions inspectable, but committee calls and cross-query memory add serving complexity.

papers.title: Exact Risk Certificates for Pairwise-Judged Reranking
papers.authors: Xinyu Wang, Jingrui Tian, Sicheng Lyu, Yu Gu, Ziyang Song, Xiao-Wen Chang, Lei Ding
papers.summary: Exact certificates bound worst-case nDCG loss using pairwise judgments, saving 2.34 comparisons per development query on shared trajectories.
papers.key_insight: Judgments constrain the ideal-ranking denominator as well as the loss numerator; ignoring that coupling wastes comparisons.

papers.title: KhyontekAI at CheckThat! 2026: Multilingual Dense Retrieval and Cross-Encoder Reranking for Scientific Web Claims
papers.summary: A metadata-enriched multilingual retriever followed by cross-encoder reranking links scientific social posts to source papers. Average MRR@5 is 0.5862.
papers.key_insight: Audit metadata, candidate depth and language balance separately to identify which parts improve source retrieval.
